Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its\n# exit code and output as the score. The interface check is separate from the conformance run so\n# that a missing or non-executable program and a genuine conformance failure are distinguishable\n# in the evidence. The program path is the harness's only knowledge of the implementation\n# language; the harness itself is language-neutral.\n#\n# The suite runs unfiltered: no --pattern, no --number, no selector of any kind. spec_tests.py\n# exits with failed + errored, so exit 0 means the complete CommonMark 0.31.2 suite passed.\nset -eu\n\nif [ ! -x ./commonmark ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./commonmark at the application root.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named commonmark that reads UTF-8 Markdown on stdin\" >&2\n    echo \"and writes HTML to stdout.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# spec_tests.py imports cmark and normalize as siblings, so the staged directory has to be on the\n# import path. The program is passed absolute because the runner spawns it from its own cwd.\nPYTHONPATH=\"$PWD/sources${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}\"\nexport PYTHONPATH\n\nset +e\noutput=$(python3 sources/spec_tests.py --program \"$PWD/commonmark\" --spec sources/spec.txt 2>&1)\nstatus=$?\nset -e\n\nprintf '%s\\n' \"$output\"\n\n# The runner exits with failed + errored, which a shell truncates modulo 256: exactly 256 or 512\n# failures would exit 0 and read as a pass. The harness therefore confirms the tally rather than\n# trusting the status alone, and reports a clean run only when both agree. This is the scoring\n# instrument reading its own instrument; the acceptance check above it still asserts nothing but\n# this script's exit code.\nif [ \"$status\" -ne 0 ]; then\n    exit 1\nfi\nif ! printf '%s\\n' \"$output\" | grep -q '0 failed, 0 errored, 0 skipped'; then\n    echo \"error: conformance runner exited 0 but did not report a clean unfiltered suite.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n----\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n\nfrom ctypes import CDLL, c_char_p, c_long, c_int\nfrom subprocess import *\nimport platform\nimport os\n\ndef pipe_through_prog(prog, text):\n    p1 = Popen(prog.split(), stdout=PIPE, stdin=PIPE, stderr=PIPE)\n    [result, err] = p1.communicate(input=text.encode('utf-8'))\n    return [p1.returncode, result, err]\n\ndef use_library(lib, text):\n    textbytes = text.encode('utf-8')\n    textlen = len(textbytes)\n    return [0, lib(textbytes, textlen, 0), '']\n\nclass CMark:\n    def __init__(self, prog=None, library_dir=None):\n        self.prog = prog\n        if prog:\n            self.to_html = lambda x: pipe_through_prog(prog, x)\n        else:\n            sysname = platform.system()\n            if sysname == 'Darwin':\n                libname = \"libcmark.dylib\"\n            elif sysname == 'Windows':\n                libname = \"cmark.dll\"\n            else:\n                libname = \"libcmark.so\"\n            if library_dir:\n                libpath = os.path.join(library_dir, libname)\n            else:\n                libpath = os.path.join(\"build\", \"src\", libname)\n            cmark = CDLL(libpath)\n            markdown = cmark.cmark_markdown_to_html\n            markdown.restype = c_char_p\n            markdown.argtypes = [c_char_p, c_long, c_int]\n            self.to_html = lambda x: use_library(markdown, x)\n----\n# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\nfrom urllib.parse import quote, unquote\n\ntry:\n    from html.parser import HTMLParseError\nexcept ImportError:\n    # HTMLParseError was removed in Python 3.5. It could never be\n    # thrown, so we define a placeholder instead.\n    class HTMLParseError(Exception):\n        pass\n\nfrom html.entities import name2codepoint\nimport sys\nimport re\nimport html\n\n# Normalization code, adapted from\n# https://github.com/karlcow/markdown-testsuite/\nsignificant_attrs = [\"alt\", \"href\", \"src\", \"title\"]\nwhitespace_re = re.compile(r\"\\s+\")\nclass MyHTMLParser(HTMLParser):\n    def __init__(self):\n        HTMLParser.__init__(self)\n        self.convert_charrefs = False\n        self.last = \"starttag\"\n        self.in_pre = False\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NeDdnLNQExg6SCEhwMkkiH","type":"tool_result","content":"----\n    5 mdparser/__init__.py\n  307 mdparser/blocks.py\n   49 mdparser/cli.py\n   96 mdparser/entities.py\n  395 mdparser/inlines.py\n    5 mdparser/refs.py\n   67 mdparser/render.py\n  924 total\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_autolinks.py\ntest_backslash_escapes.py\ntest_block_engine.py\ntest_blocks.py\ntest_code_spans.py\ntest_emphasis.py\ntest_entities.py\ntest_executable.py\ntest_foundation.py\ntest_raw_html.py\ntest_render.py\n----\n\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and `normalize_label`.\n\nResponsibility: extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes, store them in one\nreference map, and normalize labels with `str.casefold` plus whitespace collapse.\n\"\"\"\n----\n\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WFY4DVhBbhtBP89BRkxHXe","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, inlines.parse_inline)\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n----\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index:run_end])))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(Html(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index + 1])))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(Html(escape_html(value)))\n                continue\n        nodes.append(Html(escape_html(char)))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n----\n\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper and the shared destination, title and info-string helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport html.entities\nimport re\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n# A named reference: `&`, a name, then `;`. The table lookup adds the semicolon back.\nNAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);\")\n# A decimal reference has 1 to 7 digits. A hexadecimal reference has `x` or `X` and 1 to 6 digits.\nDECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#([0-9]{1,7});\")\nHEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#[xX]([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6});\")\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nMAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF\n\n\ndef match_reference(text: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded text of the character reference at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    Returns None when no recognized reference starts at `start`, so the `&` is literal text. An\n    unknown name, or a name without its semicolon, is not a reference.\n    \"\"\"\n    named = NAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if named is not None:\n        value = html.entities.html5.get(named.group(1) + \";\")\n        if value is None:\n            return None\n        return value, named.end()\n    decimal = DECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if decimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(decimal.group(1), 10)), decimal.end()\n    hexadecimal = HEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if hexadecimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(hexadecimal.group(1), 16)), hexadecimal.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _code_point_text(code_point: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the character for a numeric reference. Zero, surrogates and out-of-range values\n    become U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    if code_point == 0 or code_point > MAX_CODE_POINT or 0xD800 <= code_point <= 0xDFFF:\n        return REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER\n    return chr(code_point)\n\n\ndef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\n    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef unescape_and_decode(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes and character references to `text` in one left-to-right pass.\n\n    This is the shared helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. The pass is single\n    so that an escape is never read as the start of a reference: `\\\\&amp;` yields the literal text\n    `&amp;`, not `&`.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(text, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(value)\n                continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n----\n\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"03b536a0-4f9f-4f98-953f-a68fa7cb6fbd","uuid":"869458f2-5871-4419-a123-223809cd1a2d","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:26:58.077Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, inlines.parse_inline)\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n----\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index:run_end])))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(Html(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index + 1])))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(Html(escape_html(value)))\n                continue\n        nodes.append(Html(escape_html(char)))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n----\n\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper and the shared destination, title and info-string helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport html.entities\nimport re\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n# A named reference: `&`, a name, then `;`. The table lookup adds the semicolon back.\nNAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);\")\n# A decimal reference has 1 to 7 digits. A hexadecimal reference has `x` or `X` and 1 to 6 digits.\nDECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#([0-9]{1,7});\")\nHEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&#[xX]([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6});\")\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nMAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF\n\n\ndef match_reference(text: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded text of the character reference at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    Returns None when no recognized reference starts at `start`, so the `&` is literal text. An\n    unknown name, or a name without its semicolon, is not a reference.\n    \"\"\"\n    named = NAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if named is not None:\n        value = html.entities.html5.get(named.group(1) + \";\")\n        if value is None:\n            return None\n        return value, named.end()\n    decimal = DECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if decimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(decimal.group(1), 10)), decimal.end()\n    hexadecimal = HEXADECIMAL_REFERENCE_PATTERN.match(text, start)\n    if hexadecimal is not None:\n        return _code_point_text(int(hexadecimal.group(1), 16)), hexadecimal.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _code_point_text(code_point: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the character for a numeric reference. Zero, surrogates and out-of-range values\n    become U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    if code_point == 0 or code_point > MAX_CODE_POINT or 0xD800 <= code_point <= 0xDFFF:\n        return REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER\n    return chr(code_point)\n\n\ndef unescape(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes to `text`, for destinations, titles and info strings.\n\n    A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that character. A backslash before any other\n    character, or at the end of the text, is kept. Escapes are read left to right and each one is\n    consumed whole, so `\\\\\\\\` yields one backslash and the character after it is not escaped.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef unescape_and_decode(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Apply backslash escapes and character references to `text` in one left-to-right pass.\n\n    This is the shared helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. The pass is single\n    so that an escape is never read as the start of a reference: `\\\\&amp;` yields the literal text\n    `&amp;`, not `&`.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(text[index + 1])\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(text, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(value)\n                continue\n        out.append(char)\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n----\n\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01WFY4DVhBbhtBP89BRkxHXe","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SCPQYMqQT7Fttv51yfShQv","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the mdparser test suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nPROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef project_root() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Absolute path to the application root, where `commonmark` and `pyproject.toml` live.\"\"\"\n    return PROJECT_ROOT\n----\n\"\"\"Block-engine acceptance and end-to-end tests: paragraphs, blank lines, and HTML escaping through\nthe `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe four declared checks from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md are transcribed first, with their\nassertions unchanged. The remaining tests compare the exact stdout bytes, which is the state\nthe executable hands back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_engine_paragraph_count(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Blank-line-separated paragraphs render as one p element each.\"\"\"\n    paragraphs = [\"alpha beta\", \"gamma delta\", \"epsilon\"]\n    source = \"\\n\\n\".join(paragraphs) + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"</p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    for text in paragraphs:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_multiline_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Consecutive non-blank lines with arbitrary indentation after the first stay in one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    first = \"first line\"\n    second = \"second line\"\n    third = \"third line\"\n    source = first + \"\\n\" + \"             \" + second + \"\\n\" + third + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    for text in (first, second, third):\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_blank_lines_ignored(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Leading, trailing and repeated blank lines add no blocks; a blank-only document gives no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    word = \"content\"\n    padded = \"\\n  \\n\\n\" + word + \"\\n\\n\\n  \\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, padded)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n    blank = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\")\n    assert blank.returncode == 0\n    assert blank.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_engine_html_escaping(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Special characters in paragraph text are escaped, so only the paragraph tags contribute angle brackets.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\">\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"hello world\\n\").stdout == \"<p>hello world</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_two_paragraphs_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\n\\ntwo\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>one</p>\\n<p>two</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_multiline_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    source = \"first line\\n             second line\\nthird line\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>first line\\nsecond line\\nthird line</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_escaped_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>x &lt; y &gt; z &amp; w</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_padded_document_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n  \\n\\ncontent\\n\\n\\n  \\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>content</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_blank_only_document_output_is_empty(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\").stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_leading_and_trailing_whitespace_is_removed(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"   \\tword \\t  \\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>word</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_crlf_document_renders_the_same_as_lf(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    lf = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\ntwo\\n\\nthree\\n\")\n    crlf = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\r\\ntwo\\r\\n\\r\\nthree\\r\\n\")\n    assert lf.stdout == crlf.stdout == \"<p>one\\ntwo</p>\\n<p>three</p>\\n\"\n----\n\"\"\"Block engine tests: column helpers, the cursor, the registry, and the per-line procedure.\n\nEach test builds a block tree with `parse_lines` and reads back the tree: child block type names,\nparagraph content, and raw lines. Registry tests use block types defined here, which shows that\nthe loop never names a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks\nfrom mdparser.blocks import (\n    DOCUMENT,\n    PARAGRAPH,\n    Block,\n    BlockRegistry,\n    BlockType,\n    Cursor,\n    DocumentParser,\n    indent_columns,\n    next_column,\n    parse_lines,\n)\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_contents(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.content for child in block.children if child.kind is PARAGRAPH]\n\n\n# --- Column helpers ---\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_space_advances_one() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\" \", 3) == 4\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_tab_advances_to_next_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 0) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 2) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 4) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_pads_a_tab_after_spaces_to_the_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"  \\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_two_tabs_as_eight() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n----\n\"\"\"Renderer and inline hook tests: HTML escaping, URL percent-encoding, the phase 2 walk, and\nthe inline parser hook. Each test compares a returned string with its exact expected value.\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\nfrom mdparser.blocks import DOCUMENT, PARAGRAPH, Block, BlockRegistry, BlockType\n\n\ndef upper_hook(raw: str) -> str:\n    return raw.upper()\n\n\ndef render_source(lines: list[str], hook=inlines.parse_inline) -> str:\n    return render.render_document(blocks.parse_lines(lines), hook)\n\n\n# --- HTML escaping ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"text\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"&\", \"&amp;\"),\n        (\"<\", \"&lt;\"),\n        (\">\", \"&gt;\"),\n        ('\"', \"&quot;\"),\n        (\"'\", \"'\"),\n        (\"plain\", \"plain\"),\n        (\"\", \"\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_escape_html_maps_each_special_character(text: str, expected: str) -> None:\n    assert render.escape_html(text) == expected\n\n\ndef test_escape_html_does_not_escape_an_ampersand_twice() -> None:\n    assert render.escape_html(\"<&>\") == \"&lt;&amp;&gt;\"\n\n\ndef test_escape_html_leaves_existing_entity_text_as_an_escaped_ampersand() -> None:\n    assert render.escape_html(\"&amp;\") == \"&amp;amp;\"\n\n\n# --- URL percent-encoding ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"url\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"\", \"\"),\n        (\"abc\", \"abc\"),\n        (\"a b\", \"a%20b\"),\n        (\"é\", \"%C3%A9\"),\n        (\"😀\", \"%F0%9F%98%80\"),\n        (\"%20\", \"%20\"),\n        (\"%zz\", \"%25zz\"),\n        (\"%\", \"%25\"),\n        (\"a\\\"b\", \"a%22b\"),\n        (\"[x]\", \"%5Bx%5D\"),\n----\n\"\"\"Executable block tests: the `commonmark` entry point, input decoding, and line intake.\n\nEach test acts on the system and reads the state back: an exit status, stdout bytes, the file\nmode and shebang, or a returned value. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1f3XfJovqw8n2VvDJ21","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016pozyq8PCoYPjDfTd7DNCb","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/refs.py","content":"\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and `normalize_label`.\n\nResponsibility: extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes, store them in one\nreference map, and normalize labels with `str.casefold` plus whitespace collapse.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, unescape_and_decode\n\n# A link label may hold at most this many characters between its brackets.\nMAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 999\n# Whitespace inside a label collapses to one space: spaces, tabs and line endings.\nLABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[ \\t\\r\\n]+\")\n# Title delimiters: each opener maps to the closer that ends the title.\nTITLE_CLOSERS = {'\"': '\"', \"'\": \"'\", \"(\": \")\"}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LinkReference:\n    \"\"\"A stored definition: the decoded destination and the decoded title, or None when untitled.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n\n\ndef normalize_label(label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the matching key for a link label.\n\n    The brackets are stripped when the label has them, the text is case folded, and runs of\n    spaces, tabs and line endings collapse to one space. Matching compares these keys only.\n    \"\"\"\n    if label.startswith(\"[\") and label.endswith(\"]\"):\n        label = label[1:-1]\n    return LABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN.sub(\" \", label.casefold()).strip(\" \")\n\n\nclass ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The document-wide map from normalized label to definition. The first definition wins.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._entries: dict[str, LinkReference] = {}\n\n    def add(self, label: str, destination: str, title: str | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Store a definition under its normalized label unless that label is already present.\"\"\"\n        key = normalize_label(label)\n        if key not in self._entries:\n            self._entries[key] = LinkReference(destination, title)\n\n    def get(self, label: str) -> LinkReference | None:\n        \"\"\"The definition for `label`, matched on its normalized form, or None when absent.\"\"\"\n        return self._entries.get(normalize_label(label))\n\n    def __contains__(self, label: object) -> bool:\n        return isinstance(label, str) and normalize_label(label) in self._entries\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._entries)\n\n\ndef extract_definitions(text: str, references: ReferenceMap) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove the link reference definitions at the start of a closed paragraph's text.\n\n    Each definition found is added to `references`. Scanning stops at the first line that is not a\n    definition, and the rest of the text is returned. Text that is not at the start of the\n    paragraph is never examined, so a definition cannot interrupt a paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    pos = 0\n    while pos < len(text):\n        parsed = _parse_definition(text, pos)\n        if parsed is None:\n            break\n        label, destination, title, pos = parsed\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return text[pos:]\n\n\ndef _parse_definition(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse one definition at `pos`. Return (raw label, destination, title, index after it), or None.\"\"\"\n    label_end = _scan_label(text, pos)\n    if label_end is None:\n        return None\n    label = text[pos:label_end]\n    if text[label_end : label_end + 1] != \":\":\n        return None\n    index = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, label_end + 1)\n    destination = _parse_destination(text, index)\n    if destination is None:\n        return None\n    destination_text, after_destination = destination\n\n    destination_line_end = _line_end(text, after_destination)\n    if not _is_blank(text[after_destination:destination_line_end]):\n        # Anything after the destination on its line must be a title on that same line.\n        title_start = _skip_spaces(text, after_destination)\n        if title_start == after_destination or not _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n            return None\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is None or not _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return None\n        return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n\n    # The destination ends its line. A title may follow on a later line; if it does not parse\n    # cleanly, the definition keeps its destination and the title text stays in the paragraph.\n    title_start = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, after_destination)\n    if title_start > after_destination and _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is not None and _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n    return label, destination_text, None, _after_line(text, destination_line_end)\n\n\ndef _scan_label(text: str, pos: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the closing `]` of a link label at `pos`, or None.\n\n    The label is 1 to 999 characters between its brackets, holds no unescaped bracket, and has at\n    least one non-whitespace character.\n    \"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] != \"[\":\n        return None\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"[\":\n            return None\n        if char == \"]\":\n            inner = text[pos + 1 : index]\n            if not 1 <= len(inner) <= MAX_LABEL_LENGTH or not inner.strip():\n                return None\n            return index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded destination and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"<\":\n        return _parse_angle_destination(text, pos)\n    return _parse_plain_destination(text, pos)\n\n\ndef _parse_angle_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A destination in angle brackets: no line ending, and no unescaped `<` or `>` inside.\"\"\"\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char in \"<\\n\":\n            return None\n        if char == \">\":\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_plain_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A nonempty destination with no space or control character and balanced parentheses.\"\"\"\n    index = pos\n    depth = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"(\":\n            depth += 1\n        elif char == \")\":\n            if depth == 0:\n                break\n            depth -= 1\n        elif char == \" \" or _is_ascii_control(char):\n            break\n        index += 1\n    if index == pos or depth != 0:\n        return None\n    return unescape_and_decode(text[pos:index]), index\n\n\ndef _parse_title(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A title in double quotes, single quotes or parentheses. Return (decoded title, index past it).\"\"\"\n    opener = text[pos]\n    closer = TITLE_CLOSERS[opener]\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == closer:\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        if opener == \"(\" and char == \"(\":\n            return None\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _is_escapable(text: str, index: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the backslash at `index` escapes the character after it.\"\"\"\n    return index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION\n\n\ndef _is_title_opener(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return text[pos : pos + 1] in TITLE_CLOSERS and pos < len(text)\n\n\ndef _is_ascii_control(char: str) -> bool:\n    return char < \" \" or char == \"\\x7f\"\n\n\ndef _is_blank(segment: str) -> bool:\n    return segment.strip(\" \\t\") == \"\"\n\n\ndef _skip_spaces(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after `pos` that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n    while pos < len(text) and text[pos] in \" \\t\":\n        pos += 1\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs, then at most one line ending, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos)\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"\\n\":\n        pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos + 1)\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _line_end(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = text.find(\"\\n\", pos)\n    return len(text) if end == -1 else end\n\n\ndef _after_line(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = _line_end(text, pos)\n    return min(end + 1, len(text))\n\n\ndef _rest_of_line_is_blank(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return _is_blank(text[pos : _line_end(text, pos)])\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":17246,"cache_read_input_tokens":44720,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":17246},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"03b536a0-4f9f-4f98-953f-a68fa7cb6fbd","uuid":"91fc36a6-7af0-4570-97e4-e56453b799cc","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:28:59.463Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1f3XJDdKmUkPGMbpKgh","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_016pozyq8PCoYPjDfTd7DNCb":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/refs.py","content":"\"\"\"Link \"<\\n\":\n            return None\n        if char == \">\":\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef depth = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \\t\") == \"\"\n\n\ndef _skip_spaces(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after `pos` that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n    while pos < len(text) and text[pos] after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"","+    end = text.find(\"\\n\", pos)","+    return len(text) if end == -1 else end","+","+","+def _after_line(text: str, pos: int) -> int:","+    \"\"\"Index just past the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"","+    end = _line_end(text, pos)","+    return min(end + 1, len(text))","+","+","+def _rest_of_line_is_blank(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:","+    return _is_blank(text[pos : _line_end(text, pos)])"]}],"originalFile":"\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and
