(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"03b536a0-4f9f-4f98-953f-a68fa7cb6fbd","uuid":"f2e7fd1c-1434-47a9-a69c-f5b3c657fed8","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:29:04.561Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/refs.py","oldString":"    return text[pos : pos + 1] in TITLE_CLOSERS and pos < len(text)","newString":"    return text[pos : pos + 1] in TITLE_CLOSERS","originalFile":"\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and `normalize_label`.\n\nResponsibility: extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes, store them in one\nreference map, and normalize labels with `str.casefold` plus whitespace collapse.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, unescape_and_decode\n\n# A link label may hold at most this many characters between its brackets.\nMAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 999\n# Whitespace inside a label collapses to one space: spaces, tabs and line endings.\nLABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[ \\t\\r\\n]+\")\n# Title delimiters: each opener maps to the closer that ends the title.\nTITLE_CLOSERS = {'\"': '\"', \"'\": \"'\", \"(\": \")\"}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LinkReference:\n    \"\"\"A stored definition: the decoded destination and the decoded title, or None when untitled.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n\n\ndef normalize_label(label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the matching key for a link label.\n\n    The brackets are stripped when the label has them, the text is case folded, and runs of\n    spaces, tabs and line endings collapse to one space. Matching compares these keys only.\n    \"\"\"\n    if label.startswith(\"[\") and label.endswith(\"]\"):\n        label = label[1:-1]\n    return LABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN.sub(\" \", label.casefold()).strip(\" \")\n\n\nclass ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The document-wide map from normalized label to definition. The first definition wins.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._entries: dict[str, LinkReference] = {}\n\n    def add(self, label: str, destination: str, title: str | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Store a definition under its normalized label unless that label is already present.\"\"\"\n        key = normalize_label(label)\n        if key not in self._entries:\n            self._entries[key] = LinkReference(destination, title)\n\n    def get(self, label: str) -> LinkReference | None:\n        \"\"\"The definition for `label`, matched on its normalized form, or None when absent.\"\"\"\n        return self._entries.get(normalize_label(label))\n\n    def __contains__(self, label: object) -> bool:\n        return isinstance(label, str) and normalize_label(label) in self._entries\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._entries)\n\n\ndef extract_definitions(text: str, references: ReferenceMap) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove the link reference definitions at the start of a closed paragraph's text.\n\n    Each definition found is added to `references`. Scanning stops at the first line that is not a\n    definition, and the rest of the text is returned. Text that is not at the start of the\n    paragraph is never examined, so a definition cannot interrupt a paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    pos = 0\n    while pos < len(text):\n        parsed = _parse_definition(text, pos)\n        if parsed is None:\n            break\n        label, destination, title, pos = parsed\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return text[pos:]\n\n\ndef _parse_definition(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse one definition at `pos`. Return (raw label, destination, title, index after it), or None.\"\"\"\n    label_end = _scan_label(text, pos)\n    if label_end is None:\n        return None\n    label = text[pos:label_end]\n    if text[label_end : label_end + 1] != \":\":\n        return None\n    index = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, label_end + 1)\n    destination = _parse_destination(text, index)\n    if destination is None:\n        return None\n    destination_text, after_destination = destination\n\n    destination_line_end = _line_end(text, after_destination)\n    if not _is_blank(text[after_destination:destination_line_end]):\n        # Anything after the destination on its line must be a title on that same line.\n        title_start = _skip_spaces(text, after_destination)\n        if title_start == after_destination or not _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n            return None\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is None or not _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return None\n        return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n\n    # The destination ends its line. A title may follow on a later line; if it does not parse\n    # cleanly, the definition keeps its destination and the title text stays in the paragraph.\n    title_start = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, after_destination)\n    if title_start > after_destination and _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is not None and _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n    return label, destination_text, None, _after_line(text, destination_line_end)\n\n\ndef _scan_label(text: str, pos: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the closing `]` of a link label at `pos`, or None.\n\n    The label is 1 to 999 characters between its brackets, holds no unescaped bracket, and has at\n    least one non-whitespace character.\n    \"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] != \"[\":\n        return None\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"[\":\n            return None\n        if char == \"]\":\n            inner = text[pos + 1 : index]\n            if not 1 <= len(inner) <= MAX_LABEL_LENGTH or not inner.strip():\n                return None\n            return index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded destination and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"<\":\n        return _parse_angle_destination(text, pos)\n    return _parse_plain_destination(text, pos)\n\n\ndef _parse_angle_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A destination in angle brackets: no line ending, and no unescaped `<` or `>` inside.\"\"\"\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char in \"<\\n\":\n            return None\n        if char == \">\":\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_plain_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A nonempty destination with no space or control character and balanced parentheses.\"\"\"\n    index = pos\n    depth = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"(\":\n            depth += 1\n        elif char == \")\":\n            if depth == 0:\n                break\n            depth -= 1\n        elif char == \" \" or _is_ascii_control(char):\n            break\n        index += 1\n    if index == pos or depth != 0:\n        return None\n    return unescape_and_decode(text[pos:index]), index\n\n\ndef _parse_title(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A title in double quotes, single quotes or parentheses. Return (decoded title, index past it).\"\"\"\n    opener = text[pos]\n    closer = TITLE_CLOSERS[opener]\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == closer:\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        if opener == \"(\" and char == \"(\":\n            return None\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _is_escapable(text: str, index: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the backslash at `index` escapes the character after it.\"\"\"\n    return index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION\n\n\ndef _is_title_opener(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return text[pos : pos + 1] in TITLE_CLOSERS and pos < len(text)\n\n\ndef _is_ascii_control(char: str) -> bool:\n    return char < \" \" or char == \"\\x7f\"\n\n\ndef _is_blank(segment: str) -> bool:\n    return segment.strip(\" \\t\") == \"\"\n\n\ndef _skip_spaces(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after `pos` that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n    while pos < len(text) and text[pos] in \" \\t\":\n        pos += 1\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs, then at most one line ending, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos)\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"\\n\":\n        pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos + 1)\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _line_end(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = text.find(\"\\n\", pos)\n    return len(text) if end == -1 else end\n\n\ndef _after_line(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = _line_end(text, pos)\n    return min(end + 1, len(text))\n\n\ndef _rest_of_line_is_blank(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return _is_blank(text[pos : _line_end(text, pos)])\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":208,"oldLines":7,"newStart":208,"newLines":7,"lines":[" {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YNbrpqMqMk98kYC5uVMxSN","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"03b536a0-4f9f-4f98-953f-a68fa7cb6fbd","uuid":"bcac7395-ff1b-432a-8c4b-284af90de24e","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:29:10.124Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nTAB_STOP = 4","newString":"from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    block.content = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n    return parser.finish()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":6,"newStart":14,"newLines":8,"lines":[" from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable"," from dataclasses import dataclass"," Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    block.content = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n    return parser.finish()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":108,"oldLines":6,"newStart":108,"newLines":8,"lines":["         self.is_open = True","         self.lines: list[str] = []"," {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LseumaomTGSiQuZX7Pdd37","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"03b536a0-4f9f-4f98-953f-a68fa7cb6fbd","uuid":"9757dd0b-1a42-4a07-8d05-e521be82ed73","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:29:11.672Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"def _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    block.content = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")","newString":"def _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1f5ScjyuMjKVAGuYnhM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GGWWzks1LsdHL7WgPgMmtK","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_link_reference_definitions.py","content":"\"\"\"Link reference definitions: label normalization, the reference map, extraction at paragraph close,\nand the `commonmark` executable's output for definition-only and definition-plus-paragraph input.\n\nThe four declared checks from FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md are transcribed first, with\ntheir assertions unchanged. The remaining tests act on the parser and read the reference map or\nthe block tree back, or compare the exact stdout bytes the executable hands back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, refs\nfrom mdparser.refs import LinkReference, ReferenceMap, extract_definitions, normalize_label\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef extract(text: str) -> tuple[str, ReferenceMap]:\n    \"\"\"Run extraction on paragraph text and return the remainder and the map it filled.\"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    remainder = extract_definitions(text, references)\n    return remainder, references\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_defs_definition_only_renders_nothing(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A document that is only a definition, with or without a title or angle brackets, renders no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    for source in ['[foo]: /url \"title\"\\n', \"[foo]:\\n/url\\n'title'\\n\", \"[foo]: <>\\n\"]:\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_defs_remainder_is_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Text after a definition stays as one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    rest = \"remaining text\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"[foo]: /url\\n\" + rest + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert rest in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_trailing_text_not_definition(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Extra text after the title means the line is not a definition, so it stays a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, '[foo]: /url \"title\" ok\\n')\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_defs_cannot_interrupt_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A definition line directly after paragraph text is part of that paragraph.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"[bar]: /baz\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n\" + definition + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert definition in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_title_with_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A title containing a blank line is not valid, so the two halves become two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"[foo]: /url 'title\\n\\nwith blank line'\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\n# --- normalize_label ---\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_strips_the_brackets() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_leaves_an_unbracketed_label_unchanged() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"foo\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_applies_case_folding() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[Foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_folds_sharp_s_to_ss() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[ẞ]\") == normalize_label(\"[SS]\") == \"ss\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_collapses_internal_whitespace_to_one_space() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[foo  \\t bar\\nbaz]\") == \"foo bar baz\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_strips_outer_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[  foo  ]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_keeps_internal_punctuation() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[a-b_c]\") == \"a-b_c\"\n\n\n# --- ReferenceMap ---\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_starts_empty() -> None:\n    assert len(ReferenceMap()) == 0\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_get_returns_none_for_an_absent_label() -> None:\n    assert ReferenceMap().get(\"foo\") is None\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_stores_destination_and_title() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\", \"title\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"title\")\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_stores_an_untitled_definition_with_no_title() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_matches_on_normalized_labels() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[Foo   Bar]\", \"/url\")\n    assert references.get(\"[foo bar]\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_first_definition_wins() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/first\")\n    references.add(\"[FOO]\", \"/second\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/first\", None)\n    assert len(references) == 1\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_contains_checks_the_normalized_label() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\")\n    assert \"FOO\" in references\n    assert \"bar\" not in references\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_contains_rejects_non_strings() -> None:\n    assert 3 not in ReferenceMap()\n\n\ndef test_reference_maps_are_independent() -> None:\n    first = ReferenceMap()\n    first.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\")\n    assert len(ReferenceMap()) == 0\n\n\n# --- Extraction: the definition grammar ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_text_has_no_definitions_and_no_remainder() -> None:\n    assert extract(\"\") == (\"\", ReferenceMap())\n\n\ndef test_single_definition_consumes_all_text() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"title_source\", \"title\"),\n    [\n        ('\"title\"', \"title\"),\n        (\"'title'\", \"title\"),\n        (\"(title)\", \"title\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_title_may_use_double_single_or_parenthesized_delimiters(title_source: str, title: str) -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(f\"[foo]: /url {title_source}\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", title)\n\n\ndef test_title_may_span_lines() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url 'line one\\nline two'\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"line one\\nline two\")\n\n\ndef test_title_may_follow_the_destination_after_a_line_ending() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]:\\n/url\\n'title'\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"title\")\n\n\ndef test_title_on_a_later_line_is_not_taken_when_it_has_trailing_text() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract('[foo]: /url\\n\"title\" ok')\n    assert remainder == '\"title\" ok'\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_a_failed_title_leaves_the_destination_line_as_the_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url\\n'title\\nnot closed\")\n    assert remainder == \"'title\\nnot closed\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_title_must_be_separated_from_the_destination_by_whitespace() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract('[foo]: <>\"title\"')\n    assert remainder == '[foo]: <>\"title\"'\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_tab_is_accepted_as_separator_before_a_title() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]:\\t/url\\t'title'\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"title\")\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_may_be_empty() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: <>\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"\", None)\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_may_contain_spaces() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: <my url>\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"my url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_cannot_hold_a_line_ending() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: <my\\nurl>\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo]: <my\\nurl>\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_cannot_hold_an_unescaped_less_than() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: <a<b>\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo]: <a<b>\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_may_hold_an_escaped_less_than() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: <a\\\\<b>\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"a<b\", None)\n\n\ndef test_plain_destination_with_balanced_parentheses_is_kept_whole() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url(a)\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url(a)\", None)\n\n\ndef test_plain_destination_with_unbalanced_parenthesis_is_not_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url(a\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo]: /url(a\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_plain_destination_with_an_escaped_parenthesis_is_kept() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: /url\\\\(a\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url(a\", None)\n\n\ndef test_plain_destination_cannot_hold_a_space() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: /a b\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo]: /a b\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_plain_destination_is_unescaped() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: /a\\\\_b\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/a_b\", None)\n\n\ndef test_destination_entity_is_decoded() -> None:\n    _, references = extract(\"[foo]: /a&amp;b\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/a&b\", None)\n\n\ndef test_title_entity_is_decoded() -> None:\n    _, references = extract('[foo]: /u \"&quot;x&quot;\"')\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/u\", '\"x\"')\n\n\ndef test_destination_with_no_text_is_not_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]:\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo]:\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_label_with_an_unescaped_bracket_is_not_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[fo[o]]: /url\")\n    assert remainder == \"[fo[o]]: /url\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_label_with_an_escaped_bracket_is_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[fo\\\\[o]: /url\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert len(references) == 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"label\", [\"[]\", \"[ ]\", \"[\\t\\n]\"])\ndef test_label_with_no_non_whitespace_character_is_not_a_definition(label: str) -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(f\"{label}: /url\")\n    assert remainder == f\"{label}: /url\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_label_of_999_characters_is_a_definition() -> None:\n    label = \"a\" * 999\n    remainder, references = extract(f\"[{label}]: /url\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(label) == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_label_of_1000_characters_is_not_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(f\"[{'a' * 1000}]: /url\")\n    assert remainder == f\"[{'a' * 1000}]: /url\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_label_without_a_colon_is_not_a_definition() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo] /url\")\n    assert remainder == \"[foo] /url\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_line_after_a_definition_is_extracted_too() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[a]: /1\\n[b]: /2\\ntext\")\n    assert remainder == \"text\"\n    assert references.get(\"a\") == LinkReference(\"/1\", None)\n    assert references.get(\"b\") == LinkReference(\"/2\", None)\n\n\ndef test_first_definition_for_a_normalized_label_wins_within_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[a]: /1\\n[A]: /2\")\n    assert remainder == \"\"\n    assert references.get(\"a\") == LinkReference(\"/1\", None)\n\n\ndef test_text_before_a_definition_stops_extraction() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"Foo\\n[bar]: /baz\")\n    assert remainder == \"Foo\\n[bar]: /baz\"\n    assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_remainder_keeps_its_own_line_structure() -> None:\n    remainder, _ = extract(\"[foo]: /url\\nline one\\nline two\")\n    assert remainder == \"line one\\nline two\"\n\n\n# --- Extraction through the block tree ---\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_of_only_definitions_leaves_the_tree() -> None:\n    root = blocks.parse_lines([\"[foo]: /url\", \"[bar]: /baz\"])\n    assert root.children == []\n    assert root.references is not None\n    assert root.references.get(\"bar\") == LinkReference(\"/baz\", None)\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_remainder_becomes_its_content() -> None:\n    root = blocks.parse_lines([\"[foo]: /url\", \"remaining text\"])\n    assert [child.content for child in root.children] == test_definition_after_a_blank_line_starts_a_new_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = blocks.parse_lines([\"Foo\", \"\", \"[bar]: /baz\"])\n    assert [child.content for child in root.children] == == 1\n\n\ndef test_defs_cannot_interrupt_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A definition line directly after paragraph text is part of that paragraph.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"[bar]: /baz\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n\" + definition + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert definition in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_title_with_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A title containing a blank line is not valid, so the two halves become two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    result test_normalize_label_strips_the_brackets() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_leaves_an_unbracketed_label_unchanged() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"foo\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_applies_case_folding() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[Foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_folds_sharp_s_to_ss() assert len(ReferenceMap()) == 0\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_get_returns_none_for_an_absent_label() -> None:\n    assert ReferenceMap().get(\"foo\") is None\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_stores_destination_and_title() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\", \"title\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_matches_on_normalized_labels() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[Foo test_reference_map_contains_checks_the_normalized_label() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\")\n    assert \"FOO\" in references\n    assert \"bar\" not in references\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_contains_rejects_non_strings() -> None:\n    assert 3 not in ReferenceMap()\n\n\ndef test_reference_maps_are_independent() -> None:\n    first = references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"title\")\n\n\ndef test_title_on_a_later_line_is_not_taken_when_it_has_trailing_text() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract('[foo]: assert len(references) == 0\n\n\ndef test_angle_bracket_destination_cannot_hold_an_unescaped_less_than() -> None:\n    remainder, references = extract(\"[foo]: <a<b>\")\n    assert remainder == angle brackets, renders no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    for source in ['[foo]: /url \"title\"\\n', \"[foo]:\\n/url\\n'title'\\n\", \"[foo]: <>\\n\"]:\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_defs_remainder_is_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Text after a definition stays as one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    rest = \"remaining text\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"[foo]: /url\\n\" + rest + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert rest in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_trailing_text_not_definition(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Extra text after the title means the line is == 1\n\n\ndef test_defs_cannot_interrupt_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A definition line directly after paragraph text is part of that paragraph.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"[bar]: The remaining tests act on the parser and read the reference map or\nthe block tree back, or compare the exact stdout bytes the executable hands back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, refs\nfrom mdparser.refs import LinkReference, ReferenceMap, extract_definitions, normalize_label\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef extract(text: str) -> tuple[str, ReferenceMap]:\n    \"\"\"Run extraction on paragraph text and return the remainder and the map it filled.\"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    remainder = extract_definitions(text, references)\n    return remainder, references\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_defs_definition_only_renders_nothing(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A document that is only a definition, with or without a title or angle brackets, renders no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    for source in ['[foo]: /url \"title\"\\n', \"[foo]:\\n/url\\n'title'\\n\", \"[foo]: <>\\n\"]:\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_defs_remainder_is_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Text after a definition stays as one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    rest = \"remaining text\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"[foo]: /url\\n\" + rest + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert rest in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_trailing_text_not_definition(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Extra text after the title means the line is not a definition, so it stays a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, '[foo]: /url \"title\" ok\\n')\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_defs_cannot_interrupt_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A definition line directly after paragraph text is part of that paragraph.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"[bar]: /baz\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n\" + definition + \"\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert definition in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_defs_title_with_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A title containing a blank line is not valid, so the two halves become two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"[foo]: /url 'title\\n\\nwith blank line'\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\n# --- normalize_label ---\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_strips_the_brackets() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_leaves_an_unbracketed_label_unchanged() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"foo\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_applies_case_folding() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[Foo]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_folds_sharp_s_to_ss() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[ẞ]\") == normalize_label(\"[SS]\") == \"ss\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_collapses_internal_whitespace_to_one_space() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[foo  \\t bar\\nbaz]\") == \"foo bar baz\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_strips_outer_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[  foo  ]\") == \"foo\"\n\n\ndef test_normalize_label_keeps_internal_punctuation() -> None:\n    assert normalize_label(\"[a-b_c]\") == \"a-b_c\"\n\n\n# --- ReferenceMap ---\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_starts_empty() -> None:\n    assert len(ReferenceMap()) == 0\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_get_returns_none_for_an_absent_label() -> None:\n    assert ReferenceMap().get(\"foo\") is None\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_stores_destination_and_title() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\", \"title\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", \"title\")\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_stores_an_untitled_definition_with_no_title() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/url\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_matches_on_normalized_labels() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[Foo   Bar]\", \"/url\")\n    assert references.get(\"[foo bar]\") == LinkReference(\"/url\", None)\n\n\ndef test_reference_map_first_definition_wins() -> None:\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    references.add(\"[foo]\", \"/first\")\n    references.add(\"[FOO]\", \"/second\")\n    assert references.get(\"foo\") == LinkReference(\"/first\", None)\n    assert len(references) == 1\n\n\ndef {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1fGDaUUuG43EVkwiTNN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Definitions indented four or more spaces are currently accepted. The spec says those are indented code, but indented code is a separate story that isn't built yet, so I'm leaving it for that story. The final state is below.\n\nRESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- mdparser/refs.py\n- mdparser/blocks.py\n- tests/test_link_reference_definitions.py\n- tests/test_foundation.py\n\nSUMMARY:\n- **`mdparser/refs.py`** holds the feature. `normalize_label` strips the brackets, applies `casefold()`, and collapses spaces, tabs and line endings. `ReferenceMap` is first-wins and matches on normalized labels. `extract_definitions` peels definitions off the start of a paragraph's text and returns the remainder. It covers the label, angle and plain destination, and title rules from the spec. Destinations and titles go through `unescape_and_decode`.\n- **`mdparser/blocks.py`** calls extraction in the paragraph finalize rule. The document-wide map lives on the root `Block`, and a paragraph with only definitions is removed from the tree. The root's `references` attribute is the handle the inline stories will read.\n- **Tests**: the four declared checks are transcribed unchanged. I also added unit tests for the grammar, the map, block-tree integration, and exact executable output. Full suite: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` gives 523 passed, 1 skipped. The skip is the foundation test's parametrize list, which is now empty.\n- **`tests/test_foundation.py`**: I removed `refs` from `NO_BEHAVIOR_MODULES`. That test asserted `refs` had no public names, which stopped being true with this step. The change follows the file's own convention for modules that gained behavior. This is an edit to an existing test, so please review it.\n- I did not run `sources/full_test.sh`. None of this step's criteria invoke the staged suite. Nothing was staged or committed.\n\nChoices I made that you may want to redirect:\n- The map sits on the root `Block`, not in a parser-level object, so `finalize` can reach it through the parent chain.\n- `normalize_label` accepts a bracketed or unbracketed label, since the spec says it strips brackets.\n- Label whitespace collapse uses space, tab, CR and LF, following the feature text, not all Unicode whitespace.\n- When a title on a later line has trailing text, the definition keeps its destination and the title text stays in the paragraph. This follows the spec example.\n\nKnown gap: a definition indented four or more spaces is accepted today. The spec makes that indented code. The fix belongs with the indented-code story, which needs to record the first line's indent before this check can be correct.\n\n<blueprint-decisions>\n[{\"spec\":\"FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md\",\"severity\":\"Low\",\"subject\":\"Reference map location and definition-only paragraph removal\",\"decision\":\"The reference map is held on the document root Block and filled by the paragraph finalize rule, so containers and the inline stories share one map without changing the finalize signature. A paragraph left empty after extraction is removed from the tree.
